rules.rule: Use only ten system scales: backgrounds, gray, gray-alpha, blue, red, amber, green, teal, purple, pink; P3 colors apply automatically on compatible screens.

Each scale except backgrounds has ten steps (100 to 1000) whose role is fixed by number, not hue: 100-300 component backgrounds (rest, hover, active), 400-600 borders (rest, hover, active), 700-800 high-contrast backgrounds (rest, hover), 900 secondary text and icons, 1000 primary text and icons.
Consume colors via CSS variables named --ds-<scale>-<step> (e.g. --ds-gray-400, --ds-blue-700), never hardcoded values.
Place pages and components on Background 1 (--ds-background-100), especially under color; reserve Background 2 (--ds-background-200) for discreet, rare differentiation.
On a component placed on Background 1, shift states by one step: gray-100 on hover, gray-200 on active; small elements (badges) use gray-200 or gray-300 as background.
Opaque gray by default for text, icons, fills, borders, and separators; gray-alpha only when the background must show through (shadows, overlays, edges blending into surface).
Do not layer two alpha borders: intersections become darker; an internal separator stays inside the container border.
Material shadows remain translucent; an opaque shadow leaves a visible gray halo on backgrounds.
Compose in Geist Sans (interface, text, numbers) and Geist Mono (code, commands, paths, short identifiers); Geist Serif and Geist Pixel are display families, not interface.
Use Mono only for the identifier itself, never for the entire phrase or table containing it.
Use predefined text classes (size, line-height, letter-spacing, and weight grouped) instead of arbitrary sizes or weights; the final number of the class is the size in pixels.
Page and section headings: heading-72 to heading-14; sizes 32, 24, 20, and 16 accept the Subtle variant.
The button-16/14/12 classes are only for inside a button: 14 by default, 16 for the largest, 12 only for a mini button in a field.

Label = single-line text with comfortable line-height to align with icons; label-14 is the most common style (menus), label-13 serves as secondary line and switches to tabular figures for numbers, label-12 for tertiary in dense views.

Copy = multiline text with higher line-height than Label; copy-14 is the regular body, copy-16 for spacious views (modals), copy-13 when space is tight, copy-18 to 24 for marketing, copy-13-mono for inline code.
Get the strong variant of a class by nesting a strong element in the element carrying the class, without a new class.
Pair label-13-mono with label-14 and label-14-mono with text larger than 14 px: mono appears larger at equal size.
Surfaces placed on the page: material-base and material-small (6 px radius), material-medium and material-large (12 px radius), in increasing elevation.
Floating surfaces: material-tooltip (6 px, lightest shadow, only with a triangular point), material-menu (12 px), material-modal (12 px), material-fullscreen (16 px, maximum elevation).
Limit radii to three material values: 6, 12, and 16 px.
The grid knows three breakpoints (sm, md, lg); define columns and rows at each for predictable reflow across mobile/tablet/desktop.
Page grid: 12 columns on desktop, 6 on tablet, 4 on mobile; prose occupies 6 to 7 columns on desktop, tables and charts can span all 12.
Reserve the Grid component for visible guides on marketing and showcase pages; for a simple card grid, a plain CSS grid suffices; do not nest more than one level.
A full (solid) cell hides the guides it covers when content requires an opaque background.
Guides are decorative (aria-hidden); verify their contrast is at least 3:1 in both themes; a clickable cell has its own focus ring and follows reading order.
Each spacing has a single owner (the flow/stack/grid container); children don't add concurrent margins.
Vertical rhythm: gaps within a group at steps 2 to 4, between groups at steps 6 to 8, section changes at steps 8 to 12, step 16 reserved for major breaks.
Stillness by default: motion exists only to explain state change, preserve continuity, or confirm an action; no auto-scroll or pulsing decorative indicator.
No decorative gradients, gradient text, glows, glass, textures, or ornamental shadows; gradients only as labeled data scales.

Geist icons are distributed separately from components (@vercel/geistcn-assets); icon rules page redirects to introduction (no public rules readable on 2026-11-13). In src, don't bundle them: Material Symbols is the target.
Geist font is under SIL OFL 1.1: cite it and load from its official distribution (geist package, Google Fonts, GitHub releases); don't version its files in src.
Geist terminal themes: three neutral grades for main, secondary, and subtle text; pure black background in dark, off-white in light.
